title.narrative: International AIDS Vaccine Initiative (IAVI) core contribution 2022-2025

description.narrative:
The purpose of the renewed Danish support to IAVI is to support the organization’s work to develop effective HIV/AIDS-vaccines as described in the Impact Plan 2025. IAVI works to develop safe, effective and accessible HIV-vaccines, especially for populations in developing countries, which are less prioritized by the medical industry. So far, the medical industry has preferred to invest in medicine rather than vaccines, since the profit is higher.
By integrating scientific investigation, product development, clinical research, and a commitment to partnerships, IAVI’s Impact Plan 2025 strives to expedite the availability of a vaccine and other biomedical innovations to prevent HIV-infection and save millions of lives. To reach these objectives, IAVI’s efforts are aligned around four strategic enablers: 1) Impact-driven talent, 2) Integrated Communications, 3) Sustainable resourcing, 4) Enabling policies.

actual.value: A new multisite study, the Multisite Adolescent Girls and Young Women, MAGY, study, began at the end of 2022, to understand barriers to enrolment of adolescent girls and young women, AGYW, in future HIV prevention research, as well as product preferences and socio-behavioural factors to improve the eventual uptake of prevention products. IAVI organised a stakeholder consultation on the use of bnAbs for prevention of vertical transmission of HIV, PMTCT, held in Capetown, February 2023, to further work on a new treatment modality of HIV bnAbs for infants. The feedback gathered from this meeting will inform IAVIs clinical plans for the application of bnAbs for PMTCT The IAVI G003 trial also began in 2022 and aims to determine whether there are differences in immune responses between the US population enrolled in IAVI G002 and the African population included in G003. The first of its kind in Africa, IAVI G003 leverages mRNA technology to advance an HIV GT vaccine delivery.

actual.value:
Investigators continued through 2024 to collect end-user perspectives on HIV prevention from adolescent girls and young women in three socio-behavioural studies.
The MAGY study, launched in 2023, which aimed to engage and enrol 1200 AGYW in future HIV vaccine and antibody clinical trials in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda. The SBR component was a mixed method study to understand the factors shaping perceptions of future HIV vaccine and bnAb products, participation in related clinical trials among AGYW, and acceptability of non-traditional sampling methods. Enrolment and data collection was completed in 2024 with analysis and publication forthcoming in 2025.
IAVI has been a leader in building support and catalysing strategies to enhance access to technologies in high prevalence countries. In 2024, IAVI exploited its partnership with the Africa CDC aiming to secure a sustainable demand and supply ecosystem to support future access to mAbs in Africa. With the HIV infant Postnatal Prophylaxis (PNP) Task Force, IAVI developed an HIV PNP action plan launched in July 2024 to accelerate clinical development, regulatory approval and access to HIV bnAbs for infant prophylaxis.

target.value:
1. At least 2 germline-targeting immunogens, delivered by mRNA and/or as protein, evaluated in iterative Phase I trials in LMICs to elicit HIV broadly neutralizing antibodies.
2. Initiated (and in advanced stages) Phase I evaluation in LMICs of an HIV antigen based on mRNA technology, which is designed to elicit broad and functional T cell responses.
3. At least 1 HIV vaccine candidate advanced to late-stage testing and at least 2 novel vaccine candidates entered clinical testing with IAVI involvement.

actual.value: Development of IAVIs promising germline-targeting (GT) HIV vaccine approach continued, with four preclinical papers published in high-impact journals and ground-breaking data from IAVI G002 and G003 trials immunological endpoint analyses recently published in Science. These study results provide further proof of concept for the strategy to design HIV antigens to induce antibodies capable of developing into broadly neutralising ones (bnAbs). Next studies in humans will launch in 2025. The partners completed a regulatory submission for the groups first clinical trial to South African Health Products Regulatory Authority in Q4 2024.

actual.value:
IAVI advanced two novel HIV vaccine concepts in 4 clinical trials building on long-standing and flexible support from funders in HIV discovery and vaccine design research. Early in 2022, IAVI reported encouraging results from the IAVI G001 trial, a Phase I trial that evaluated eOD-GT8 60mer, a priming immunogen, delivered as a recombinant protein.
IAVI in collaboration with Moderna launched at the beginning of 2022 two new trials (IAVI G002 in the US and G003 in Africa), evaluating eOD-GT8 60mer, now encoded as mRNA.
two Phase I trials, IAVI W001 and IAVI C101. IAVI W001, a Phase I trial that is testing a novel HIV vaccine candidate BG505 SOSIP.664 gp140 as the first clinical trial for a native like Env trimer, began in 2019 and will be completed in Q2 2023.
